extensions.readme:
# Raised frets

A Clackpad extension that puts predicted words on the **fret bars** (the silver bars between key rows), inspired by the predictive-word-on-the-keyboard idea of classic physical-keyboard phones.

> Independent, unofficial, non-commercial fan project. See [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

## What it does

Clackpad's keyboard already knows which words are likely next. This extension only decides **how they are shown** on the frets; the keyboard supplies the candidates (an extension can never supply or read words). You choose, in the extension's options:

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Suggestions shown | 1 to 5 | 3 |
| Accept with | Tap / Flick up / Tap or flick up | Tap or flick up |
| Placement | Above the likely next letter / Spread evenly | Above the likely next letter |
| Look | Classic text / Raised plate | Raised plate |
| Keep the suggestion strip | on / off (off lets the frets replace the strip) | on |
| Font size | 8 to 18 | 12 |
| Colour | Text / Accent / Dim | Text |
| Show in landscape | on / off | on |

**Look.** "Raised plate" draws each word on a small raised plate on the bar. "Classic text" draws no plate at all: the words are small, plain, white-ish text (the board's own legend colour) sitting on the fret line, directly above the key of the letter that continues the word, with a faint halo so they read on every skin. In Classic text the size follows the key legends (about 60%, 11 to 16 sp) and the Font size option is not used. Placement, accepting by tap or flick up, and the screen-reader labels are the same in both looks.

## Permissions

`suggestions:surface` only: "Shows suggestions on the fret bars". It reads nothing you type, uses no network and writes no files.

## Install

1. Get `dev.asystemofcells.frets.raised-1.1.0.cpx` (from the catalog, or copy it to the phone).
2. Clackpad > Extensions > Browse (or From file), check the permission list, Install.
3. Open the extension and switch it on. Installing never enables it.
4. Adjust the options on the same screen. Switch it off (or "Safe mode: disable all") to get the stock frets back.

Requires the Clackpad build that implements the `frets` suggestion surface.

## How it is built

`extension.json` declares one `suggestionSurface` for the `frets` surface and eight option fields; `fromConfig` ties each surface field to the option that drives it, so the user's choice replaces the declared default at run time. There is no code in the package. Validate and pack with `clackpad/extensions-sdk` (`node validate.mjs`, `node pack.mjs`), or run `../build.sh`.

## Licence

Code and manifest: MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). The icon is original artwork drawn for this project (a small keyboard with a word on a metal bar), under the same licence. No third-party logos, fonts, trademarks or artwork are included.

notes: New "Look" option: "Raised plate" (the default, as before) or "Classic text". Classic text drops the plate: the predicted words are small, plain, medium-weight text sitting right on the fret line over the key of the letter that continues the word, with a faint halo so they read on any skin. Placement, tap and flick-up work the same in both looks.
Needs Clackpad version code 50 or newer.

First release: a `frets` suggestion surface with options for count (1 to 5), accept gesture (tap, flick up, both), placement (above the likely next letter, or evenly), keeping the suggestion strip, font size, colour and landscape.
Original icon (a small keyboard with a word on a metal bar).

extensions.readme:
# Send to Obsidian

A Clackpad extension that **sends text to your own Obsidian vault**: what you typed, or what is on the clipboard, becomes a Markdown note (or a line in a daily or single note) in a folder you choose.

> Unofficial community extension. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Obsidian. See [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

## How it works with a vault

A vault is an ordinary folder of `.md` files. You pick that folder **once** with the system folder picker, and the extension writes files into it. Obsidian notices new and changed files on its own, and syncs them the way it already syncs your vault (Obsidian Sync or any other sync you use). There is no Obsidian plugin, account, network call or API key.

If you would rather go through Obsidian itself, `obsidian://new` links also work; this extension uses `obsidian://open` only to open your vault (and optionally one note).

## The Obsidian tab

After you enable the extension, the Tools Panel gets an **Obsidian** tab:

- a status row: `Vault: <folder name>` or `Not connected`
- **Send typed text** (the selection if there is one, else the whole field)
- **Send clipboard**
- **Open vault**
- **Connect vault** (opens this extension's options)

## Options

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| Vault folder | The folder you grant, picked once. Choose a subfolder of the vault to keep sends in one place. |
| Vault name | Used only by **Open vault** (the name Obsidian shows for the vault). |
| Each send | Creates a new note / Appends to the daily note / Appends to one note |
| New note name | Template, default `{{title}}`. `{{title}}` is the first line of the text (up to 60 characters). `{{date}}`, `{{time}}`, `{{datetime}}` work too. Do not type `.md`. |
| Daily note name | Default `{{date}}`, for example `2026-11-03` |
| Single note name | Default `Clackpad inbox` |
| Add frontmatter to new notes | `created`, `source` and `tags` properties at the top of a new note |
| Tags | Comma separated, without `#`, for example `inbox, idea` |
| Note to open | Optional note for **Open vault**; the same variables work, for example `{{date}}` |

A new note never overwrites: if the name exists, the note is saved as `name (2).md`. Appended entries are added under a `## HH:mm` heading.

## Privacy

Text is read **only when you tap a button**, never from password, incognito or never-learn fields, and goes only into the folder you picked. Permissions:

| Permission | Why |
|---|---|
| `typed:read` | Send typed text |
| `clipboard` | Send clipboard |
| `folder:write` | Write into the vault folder you chose (and nowhere else) |
| `uri:obsidian` | Open vault (an `obsidian://` link) |

## Install

Clackpad > Extensions > Browse (or From file) > review the permissions > Install > open the extension, switch it on, choose the vault folder.

## Licence

Code and manifest: MIT ([LICENSE](LICENSE)). The icon is original artwork drawn for this project (a page with a downward arrow) under the same licence. It does not use the Obsidian logo or any other third-party artwork.

notes: First release: Send typed text, Send clipboard, Open vault and Connect vault from an Obsidian tab in the Tools Panel.
Modes: new note per send, append to a daily note, append to one note. Name templates with `{{title}}`, `{{date}}`, `{{time}}`, `{{datetime}}`.
